newsitem.title: INDIA: Mixed response seen for India BPCL issue.
newsitem.headline: Mixed response seen for India BPCL issue.

text.p: India's state-run refining firm Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL), unfazed by a downtrend in the primary market since January, on Tuesday announced pricing of its forthcoming 4.12 billion rupee equity issue.
Each share of 10 rupee face value would be priced at 275 rupees, a BPCL spokesman said.
Analysts said BPCL would have no problem is selling about half the issue reserved for institutional buyers, but may have problems in selling the other half to retail investors.
"We think it will be difficult to sell the issue at the retail level," said an executive of a securities firm.
"We suggested a price band of 200-225 rupees when a merchant banker interviewed us," he said. BPCL had touched a low of 220 rupees on the Bombay Stock Exchange in recent months.

Analysts said one factor which could help BPCL would be the fact that retail investors need not pay in one shot, but in four instalments. This meant that the actual public issue would be only 500 million rupees at a time, they said.
But this also meant the retail investor could sell his share only after an year.
A similar public issue of shares by Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) had attracted sizable subscriptions from companies last year.
"This year corporates may not have funds like last year," one analyst said.

Domestic institutions, banks and mutual funds have been reserved 20 percent of shares and foreign institutional investors and non-resident Indians another 20 percent. Employees have been alloted another 10 percent.
The issue would reduce government's holding in BPCL to 60.18 percent from 66.2 percent. The issue would partly finance BPCL's capital expenditure of 57.2 billion rupees up to the year 1999/2000.
"It is the first good issue to hit the market after a long time," said a broker. "Every FII (foreign institutional investor) has a buy on it," he said.
BPCL is one of India's three leading refiners with a market share of 20.3 percent during 1995/96 (April-March). Its Bombay refinery refines 7.2 million tonnes of crude annually.
